S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (dysthymia) is characterized by a chronically low mood lasting at least two years in adults, with only brief periods of remission. Individuals often function day to day but at a reduced level, experiencing the depression as part of their usual personality or life, which can delay recognition and treatment. Compared with major depressive disorder, the symptoms are typically less acute but more enduring, leading to long-term interpersonal, occupational, and quality-of-life impairment. It frequently coexists with other psychiatric conditions and may be punctuated by superimposed major depressive episodes ("double depression").

patient.stressor: For Loi, the depressive period gradually took shape after her company underwent a major restructuring a little over three years ago, increasing her claims load and shifting her from field work she enjoyed to more remote desk-based assessments. The longer hours, constant video calls, and pressure to mentor younger adjusters while learning new software left her feeling drained by the end of each day, and she began skipping her weekend hikes and painting sessions, telling herself it was just a busy season. As this "busy season" stretched into years, she noticed that even vacations to wine country and carefully planned trips abroad failed to restore her usual sense of engagement, and her husband pointed out that she no longer seemed to take pleasure in planning their outings or photographing the Temecula hills. When she started making small errors in reports and needing multiple days to complete tasks that once took an afternoon, she became worried about her performance reviews and, at the suggestion of a colleague who had sought help for burnout, she contacted her primary care physician, who recognized a longstanding mood issue and referred her to psychiatry.
patient.chief_complaint: For the past few years I feel worn out all the time, like I’m running on empty even when I’m not doing that much.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I just feel this low, heavy cloud sitting on me, like I'm going through the motions on calls and at home but everything feels a little gray and joyless, even things I used to really look forward to like planning trips or taking photos of the hills.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Even on days when I sleep a full night and barely leave my desk, I feel completely drained, like my body is filled with sand, so that by the time I log off I don't have the energy to cook dinner, return friends’ texts, or even think about pulling out my paints.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: I catch myself thinking, over and over, that this is just how my life is going to be from now on—tired, flat, and just getting through work—and that no vacation, no change in job, no medication is really going to make me feel any different.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Over the past few years my work reviews have slipped from “exceeds expectations” to just “meets,” I’ve had to stay late to fix small mistakes, and at home I mostly bow out of social plans and hobbies, which has caused tension with my husband and left me feeling like I’m just existing instead of really participating in my life.
add_requirements.duration: This worn-out, low, gray way of feeling has been hanging around pretty steadily since the big restructuring at my company a little over three years ago.
